papers.title: metaWEPP: leveraging biobank-scale intra-species phylogenies for near-haplotype resolution in metagenomic analysis.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing is transforming diverse areas of health and biological sciences, including pathogen surveillance, clinical diagnostics, and microbiome research. However, the inherent complexity of metagenomic data limits most computational tools to species-level classification and abundance estimation, overlooking within-species genetic diversity that drives key phenotypes. We present metaWEPP, a novel computational pipeline that achieves near-haplotype resolution in metagenomic analysis for species with adequate representation in reference genome biobanks and having sufficient sequenci
papers.summary: metaWEPP is a new computational pipeline that uses intra-species phylogenies from biobank-scale reference genomes to achieve near-haplotype resolution in metagenomic analysis, going beyond typical species-level classification. This allows researchers to capture within-species genetic diversity that is critical for understanding phenotypes like pathogenicity or antibiotic resistance.

papers.title: Is Ergothioneine an Important Source of Plasma Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Humans?
papers.abstract: High circulating levels of trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO), largely produced by hepatic oxidation of gut-microbiota-derived trimethylamine (TMA), are associated with increased risk of cardiometabolic and neurodegenerative diseases. In contrast, the diet-derived compound ergothioneine (ET) possesses cytoprotective and neuroprotective properties, and higher circulating ET levels have been linked to a lower risk of cardiovascular, neurodegenerative, and other age-related disorders. However, concerns have been raised that microbial degradation of ET may also contribute to the TMAO pool. In this stud
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the dietary compound ergothioneine (ET), which has protective health effects, can be converted by gut microbes into trimethylamine (TMA) and subsequently into TMAO, a metabolite linked to disease risk. The findings suggest that ET is not a significant source of TMAO in humans, alleviating concerns that its beneficial effects might be offset by TMAO production.

papers.title: Dynamics of the magnum microbiome and predicted metabolic pathways across the egg-laying cycle in commercial laying hens.
papers.abstract: The microbiome of a chicken's reproductive tract is essential for egg production and safety. It helps regulate the immune system, preventing the transmission of pathogens like Salmonella and Staphylococcus that can contaminate eggs and pose health risks. Older hens may experience reduced immune function, which can disrupt their microbiome and increase the likelihood of harmful bacterial growth. We hypothesize that age-related shifts in the oviduct microbiome influence egg production and safety. This study aims to identify microbial communities and predicted pathways in the magnum of laying hen
papers.summary: This study investigates how the microbiome of the magnum (a section of the oviduct) changes with age in laying hens and how these shifts may affect egg production and safety. The researchers identified specific microbial communities and predicted metabolic pathways, suggesting that age-related microbiome disruptions could increase the risk of pathogen transmission to eggs. The findings provide insights into improving egg safety by managing the reproductive tract microbiome in older hens.

papers.title: Strain-level ecological filtering governs microbial colonization of the human gut.
papers.abstract: Microbial colonization of the human gut is typically inferred from species-level profiling, yet durable establishment operates at the strain level. Here, using longitudinal shotgun metagenomics across multiple donor-recipient pairs undergoing fecal microbiota transplantation, we show that colonization is governed by lineage-dependent strain-level ecological filtering. Strain-resolved analyses reveal that gut colonization imposes reproducible population-genetic bottlenecks, characterized by reduced nucleotide diversity and selective strain capture. Lineage identity is the primary determinant of
papers.summary: This study uses longitudinal metagenomic data from fecal microbiota transplant recipients to show that microbial colonization of the human gut is governed by strain-level ecological filtering, not just species-level dynamics. The authors find that colonization imposes reproducible population-genetic bottlenecks, with lineage identity being the primary determinant of which strains successfully establish.

papers.title: Comparative metagenomic assessment of Illumina-compatible library preparation methods, short-read lengths, and PacBio HiFi sequencing reveals differences in microbial and functional diversity recovery from a complex environmental sample.
papers.abstract: Metagenomics enables comprehensive exploration of microbial communities but is influenced by library preparation and sequencing technologies, affecting recovery of microbial genomes and proteins. Here, we benchmarked six Illumina-compatible short-read library preparation conditions in triplicate at 2 × 150 bp and 2 × 250 bp read lengths alongside PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing using a composite environmental sample of marine mangrove sediment and terrestrial palm tree soil. Longer short reads (2 × 250 bp) combined with optimal library preparation approaches improved assembly quality, protein
papers.summary: This study compares different library preparation methods and sequencing read lengths (short-read Illumina and PacBio HiFi long-read) for metagenomic analysis of a complex environmental sample. The authors find that longer short reads (2x250 bp) combined with optimal library preparation improve assembly quality and recovery of microbial genomes and functional proteins.

papers.title: Environmental emergence and dissemination of clinically relevant multidrug-resistant bacteria and resistance genes in sewage and aquatic ecosystems.
papers.abstract: This study characterized multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria in sewage, river, and marine ecosystems in South Gujarat, India.
papers.journal: Osong public health and research perspectives
papers.summary: This study characterizes multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria and resistance genes in sewage, river, and marine ecosystems in South Gujarat, India, highlighting how these environments can serve as reservoirs and pathways for the spread of clinically relevant resistance. The findings underscore the role of environmental contamination in the dissemination of antibiotic resistance, which poses a public health risk.

papers.title: The need for standardization and improved open (meta)data practices in metaproteomics.
papers.abstract: Metaproteomics enables functional insight into microbial communities by identifying and quantifying proteins in complex samples. Yet, heterogeneous analytical workflows and the lack of standardization across experimental and bioinformatics stages hinder reproducibility and comparability, limiting integration with other omics data. We here present a community-developed reporting checklist tailored to the specific needs of metaproteomics. We also outline current efforts to enable structured and interoperable metadata capture, drawing on standards from proteomics and microbiome research wherever
papers.summary: This paper highlights that inconsistent methods and lack of standardization in metaproteomics hinder reproducibility and integration with other omics data. The authors present a community-developed reporting checklist and outline efforts to improve structured metadata capture by leveraging existing standards from proteomics and microbiome research.

papers.title: Molecular and phenotypic profiles of carbapenem- and third-generation cephalosporin-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from the fecal microbiota of pediatric patients with COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Gut colonization with multidrug-resistant (MDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae is commonly associated with an increased risk of extraintestinal infections among hospitalized patients. Extensive antibiotic exposure during the COVID-19 pandemic, is a critical contributing factor for the emergence of resistant strains. This investigation sought to elucidate the phenotypic and molecular resistance traits of carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae (CRKP) and extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing K. pneumoniae (ESBL-KP) colonizing the gut of pediatric patients with confirmed COVID-19.
papers.summary: This study characterizes antibiotic-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains found in the gut of children with COVID-19, revealing that extensive antibiotic use during the pandemic promoted the spread of carbapenem-resistant and ESBL-producing strains. The findings highlight the need for antimicrobial stewardship in pediatric COVID-19 care.

papers.title: Causal Relationships Between Oral Microbiota and Inflammatory Skin Diseases.
papers.abstract: The oral microbiome has been increasingly linked to systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation, but whether specific oral bacteria causally contribute to inflammatory skin diseases remains unclear due to confounding and reverse causation. This study aimed to assess the causal effects of 43 oral microbiota taxa on the risk of five inflammatory skin diseases using a Mendelian randomization (MR) approach.
papers.summary: This study used Mendelian randomization to investigate whether specific oral bacteria causally influence the risk of inflammatory skin diseases, finding evidence for causal relationships that are not explained by confounding or reverse causation. The results suggest that certain oral microbiota taxa may play a role in the development of these skin conditions.

papers.title: Taxonomic and Functional Comparative Metagenomics of Peruvian Salterns: Insights into Microbial Communities and Aminotransferase Potential.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic analysis of extreme environments is essential in biotechnological research. This work aimed to determine and compare the microbial diversity of two Peruvian saline environments and characterise their functional profiles. Soil metagenomic DNA (mDNA) was analysed from Maras and Pilluana salterns, both with a thalassohaline origin but with different geographical and environmental conditions. Maras samples exhibited more diversity and a remarkably higher abundance of archaea (phylum Euryarchaeota). The most dominant bacterial phyla across all the samples were Pseudomonadota and Actinom
papers.summary: This study compares the microbial diversity and functional potential of two Peruvian salterns, revealing that Maras samples have higher archaeal abundance (Euryarchaeota) while Pseudomonadota and Actinobacteria dominate bacterial communities. The work highlights how different environmental conditions shape microbial composition and identifies aminotransferase-related genes as biotechnologically relevant.

papers.title: Pine-Extracted Volatile Oils Suppress Root Rot in Psammosilene tunicoides Through Direct Antifungal Activity and Rhizosphere Microbiome Modulation.
papers.abstract: Frequent outbreaks of root rot in Psammosilene tunicoides W. C. Wu & C. Y. Wu severely compromise the quality of its medicinal materials and hinder its large-scale cultivation. Interestingly, wild P. tunicoides growing under pine trees rarely experience this disease. To explore the potential basis of root rot suppression, we evaluated the direct antifungal activity of pine-derived volatile oils and the associated changes in the rhizosphere microbiome. GC-MS showed that pine turpentine was dominated by α-pinene (45.50%) and longifolene (28.20%). In vitro assays confirmed its highly efficient in
papers.summary: This study investigates why wild Psammosilene tunicoides plants growing under pine trees rarely suffer from root rot, finding that pine-derived volatile oils (especially α-pinene and longifolene) directly inhibit fungal pathogens and also reshape the rhizosphere microbiome to suppress disease. The results suggest that pine volatile oils could serve as a natural, dual-action strategy for controlling root rot in medicinal plant cultivation.

papers.title: Changes in the Gut Microbiome Following Perioperative Prophylactic Cefazolin Administration in Patients Undergoing Orthopedic Surgery: A Longitudinal Prospective Study.
papers.abstract: Cefazolin is a first-generation cephalosporin with a moderate antimicrobial spectrum and the ability to induce the production of beta-lactamases by bacterial hosts. We investigated the effect of prophylactic cefazolin administration on the gut microbiome in patients undergoing orthopedic surgery.
papers.summary: This study examines how a single dose of the antibiotic cefazolin, given before orthopedic surgery to prevent infection, alters the gut microbiome over time. The researchers found significant changes in the composition of gut bacteria following administration, suggesting that even short-term antibiotic prophylaxis can disrupt the microbiome.

papers.title: D2O-Enabled Chemical Beaconing: Tracking Steroid Metabolism by Pooled Gut Microbiota.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota actively metabolizes steroid hormones, but the mechanisms of these transformations-particularly the sequence of enzymatic reactions and the source of hydrogen atoms-remain poorly understood. Conventional analytical approaches are hampered by the complex fecal matrix, isomeric metabolites, and the lack of authentic reference standards. Here we present a strategy based on parallel incubation of steroids with pooled human gut microbiota in H2O and D2O, followed by HPLC-HRMS, with the aim of determining the sequence of reductive steps and tracking the incorporation of atoms into
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new method using heavy water (D2O) to track how gut bacteria metabolize steroid hormones, solving the problem of complex fecal samples and missing reference standards. By incubating steroids in both normal and heavy water and analyzing with mass spectrometry, researchers can determine the order of chemical reactions and where hydrogen atoms come from during metabolism.

papers.title: Using Gut Microbiota and Gut Metabolites as Biomarkers for Diseases in Monogastric Farm Animals.
papers.abstract: The use of biomarkers as diagnostic tools for animal health is becoming an increasingly important resource. In particular, this is true for digestive conditions, where an analysis of fecal samples can provide a non-invasive source of material for analysis. These samples can be used for the early detection of developing conditions or where an infection has taken place. However, biomarkers can also be used as a predictive tool for the advanced identification of animals that may be at an increased risk of developing a condition or having increased susceptibility to a particular type of infection.
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of gut microbiota and metabolites from fecal samples as non-invasive biomarkers for diagnosing and predicting diseases in monogastric farm animals. It highlights the potential for early detection of digestive conditions and identification of animals at increased risk of infection.

papers.title: A Validated LC-MS/MS Method for Quantifying Phenolic Acids, Lignans, and Enterolignans from Human Fecal Samples.
papers.abstract: The human gut is home to numerous small molecules that impact health. Three prominent classes of molecules in this environment are phenolic acids, lignans, and enterolignans, which have been linked to anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects as well as protection from cancer, cardiovascular disease, and neurodegeneration. The abundance of these molecules in the intestine as well as their biological significance motivated the development and validation of the LC-MS/MS method reported herein, which provides a simple, robust, and high-throughput approach to simultaneously quantify a 22-membered
papers.summary: This paper reports a new LC-MS/MS method for simultaneously measuring 22 phenolic acids, lignans, and enterolignans in human fecal samples. The method is validated as simple, robust, and high-throughput, enabling better study of these gut metabolites linked to anti-inflammatory and protective health effects.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Viral Communities in Hospital, University and Urban Wastewater by Shotgun Metagenomic Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance has emerged as a powerful approach for population-level monitoring of pathogen circulation in a timely and non-invasive manner. In this study, shotgun metagenomic sequencing was applied to wastewater samples collected from a hospital (HP), a university campus (UN), and a wastewater treatment plant (WTP). Viral sequences were taxonomically classified using Kraken2. Specifically, HP samples showed the highest viral richness, followed by WTP and UN samples (HP vs. UN, p = 0.0003; WTP vs. UN, p = 0.0018). Using Jaccard distance, significant differences were observed b
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare viral communities in wastewater from a hospital, university, and treatment plant, finding that hospital wastewater had the highest viral richness. The results highlight how different wastewater sources harbor distinct viral profiles, which can inform targeted surveillance strategies.

papers.title: Composting Restructures Chicken Manure Viral Communities and Attenuates Virus-Associated Antibiotic Resistance Signals: Paired Metagenome and Virome Analyses.
papers.abstract: Composting is widely used to reduce biological risks during manure recycling, but changes in viral communities and virus-associated antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) remain poorly resolved. This study aimed to assess changes in DNA viral communities, eukaryotic viral protein signals, virus-associated ARGs, and predicted virus-host linkages during chicken manure composting using paired analyses of total-community metagenomes and viral-particle-enriched viromes. Both approaches recovered viral assemblages dominated by Uroviricota and lytic viruses but produced distinct profiles. Viromes yielded
papers.summary: Composting chicken manure significantly alters viral communities and reduces virus-associated antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), as shown by paired metagenome and virome analyses. The study found that composting shifts viral composition toward lytic viruses and attenuates ARG signals linked to viruses, highlighting a potential mechanism for reducing antibiotic resistance spread during manure recycling.

papers.title: Cold Exposure Shifts Gut Microbial Butyrate Synthesis Toward the Lysine-Dependent and But-Mediated Terminal Pathways to Enhance Cold Tolerance in Min Pigs.
papers.abstract: This study combined seasonal observation in Min pigs and acute cold challenge experiments in Min pigs and Large White pigs to analyze changes in gut butyrate synthesis under cold exposure and its association with thermogenesis. Compared with summer, Min pigs in winter showed significantly higher Bacteroidota abundance (p = 0.006), lysine-pathway genes (p < 0.05), and relative gene abundance of the but terminal pathway (p < 0.05). Fecal (47.96 vs. 40.24 µmol/L, p = 0.020) and serum (4.64 vs. 2.17 µmol/L, p = 0.046) butyrate were also elevated and correlated with 10 thermogenesis-related genes (
papers.summary: This study shows that cold exposure alters the gut microbiome of Min pigs, increasing butyrate production via specific metabolic pathways, which correlates with enhanced thermogenesis and cold tolerance. The findings suggest a mechanistic link between gut microbial butyrate synthesis and host adaptation to cold environments.

papers.title: Microbial Inulinases: Characterization, Properties, and Potential Contribution to Metabolic and Nutritional Health.
papers.abstract: Microbial inulinases are enzymes produced by bacteria, yeasts, and fungi that can hydrolyze inulin into fructose and fructooligosaccharides (FOSs). The article discusses the various types of inulinases (exo- and endo-inulinases), microbial sources, biochemical properties, and optimal activity conditions, which are critical for their use in biotechnological and food processes. Special emphasis is placed on inulin degradation products, particularly FOSs, which are known for their prebiotic properties. They promote the growth of beneficial intestinal microbiota, helping to maintain digestive heal
papers.summary: This review examines microbial inulinases, enzymes that break down inulin into prebiotic fructooligosaccharides (FOSs) and fructose. It covers the types, sources, and optimal conditions of these enzymes, highlighting their potential to produce FOSs that support beneficial gut bacteria and digestive health.

papers.title: Beyond the Human Binary: Decoding Hormone-Immune Plasticity in Transgender Health.
papers.abstract: Sex- and gender-based immune differences have often been interpreted through a male-female biological binary, overlooking how endocrine signaling dynamically shapes immune function. Gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) offers a unique physiological model to disentangle the effects of sex steroids from chromosomal background and examine immune plasticity in contexts relevant to reproductive health. This hormone-informed framework proposes that estradiol and testosterone regulate immune set-points across innate, adaptive, metabolic, and mucosal compartments. Through genomic and non-genomic si
papers.summary: This paper argues that the traditional male-female binary view of immune differences is insufficient, and instead proposes a framework where hormones like estradiol and testosterone dynamically shape immune function. Using gender-affirming hormone therapy as a model, the authors explore how sex steroids regulate immune plasticity across various compartments, independent of chromosomal background.

papers.title: Fecal calprotectin and gut microbiome in a cohort without intestinal pathologies from northern Italy.
papers.abstract: Fecal calprotectin is a biomarker for intestinal inflammatory conditions, while specific taxa of gut microbiota are proposed as biomarkers for inflammatory bowel disease. However, the relationship between microbiota and calprotectin levels is still largely unexplored. Using shallow shotgun metagenomics, we investigate microbial taxonomic and functional patterns correlated with calprotectin levels in fecal samples of 515 adult individuals without known intestinal pathologies, enrolled within the Parma Microbiota Project. The median value of calprotectin was 23.6 μg/g, but levels higher than the
papers.summary: This study examines the relationship between fecal calprotectin levels and gut microbiome composition in 515 adults without known intestinal diseases. Using shallow shotgun metagenomics, they found that even in healthy individuals, higher calprotectin levels correlate with specific microbial taxonomic and functional patterns, suggesting a baseline interaction between gut inflammation markers and microbiota.

papers.title: Feasibility and Compliance of Stool Collection for Future Microbiome-Based Colorectal Cancer Screening: Preliminary Findings from a Prospective Multicenter FIT-Positive Cohort.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, and early detection through population-based screening programs significantly reduces both incidence and mortality. Although gut microbiome-based biomarkers have emerged as promising non-invasive tools for CRC detection, limited evidence is available regarding patient acceptance and compliance with microbiome-based screening studies, factors that may influence their future implementation in clinical practice. We conducted a preliminary analysis of an ongoing multicenter, prospective observational study designed to develop a gut micr
papers.summary: This study assesses patient willingness to provide stool samples for microbiome-based colorectal cancer screening, finding high compliance and feasibility in a prospective cohort. The results support the potential for integrating microbiome biomarkers into routine screening programs.

papers.title: Pilot Study on the Use of Low-Field Nuclear Magnetic Resonance as a Noninvasive Tool for Monitoring Mucus in Obstructive Lung Diseases.
papers.abstract: Patients with muco-obstructive lung disease (MOLD) exhibit chronic bronchitis and inflammation, along with a progressive decline in lung function. Lung monitoring is typically performed using spirometry, especially by measuring the forced expired volume in the first second (FEV1). However, the limitations of spirometry motivated the exploration of alternative approaches. The spin-spin relaxation time (T2m) and the spin-lattice relaxation time (T1m) of sputum water hydrogens were measured using low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) in 38 MOLD patients and 16 controls. The levels of TNFα
papers.summary: This pilot study explores low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) as a noninvasive tool to monitor mucus in patients with muco-obstructive lung diseases, measuring relaxation times of sputum water hydrogens. The findings suggest LF-NMR could complement spirometry by providing additional information on mucus properties, potentially improving disease monitoring.

papers.title: Assessment of Stability of Preservation Techniques for Strawberry Soil Microbiomes: Exploring the Biotechnological Relevance for Sustainable Agriculture.
papers.abstract: Preserving ex situ soil microbial communities is essential for bacterial biodiversity conservation in microbiome biobanking, accurate microbiome research, and future biotechnological applications in sustainable agriculture. The effect of three soil preservation methods-cryopreservation at -80 °C, refrigeration at 4 °C, and lyophilization-on the viability, diversity and metabolic functionality of the soil microbiome was evaluated using soil from untreated and solarized strawberry fields stored at 0, 6 and 12 months. Microbial viability, ecological strategies, functionality, and diversity were a
papers.summary: This study evaluates how different soil preservation methods (cryopreservation, refrigeration, and lyophilization) affect the viability, diversity, and metabolic functionality of strawberry soil microbiomes over time. The findings provide guidance for maintaining soil microbial communities for biobanking and sustainable agriculture applications.

papers.title: Evaluating the Effect of Sampling Scale on Mosquito Virome Characterization Using PacBio HiFi Long-Read Metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Characterizing the mosquito virome is essential for understanding host-microbiota interactions and vector competence, but it can be influenced by sample scale, sequencing strategy, and host depletion. This study evaluated the effect of sampling scale on mosquito virome characterization using a third-generation sequencing (TGS) metagenomics approach based on PacBio HiFi long reads, applied to L4 larvae and adults of Aedes mariae, analyzing single individuals and pools of increasing size before and after host genome removal. The results showed that sequencing yield did not increase with pool siz
papers.summary: This study tested how the number of mosquitoes pooled together affects the detection of viruses in the mosquito virome using PacBio long-read sequencing. They found that sequencing yield did not increase with larger pool sizes, and that host genome removal improved virus detection. The work provides practical guidance for designing mosquito virome studies.

papers.title: Microbial Community Differentiation and Predicted Chemical-Defense-Related Functional Potential Across Distinct Microhabitats of Cultured Hemicentrotus pulcherrimus.
papers.abstract: Sea urchins harbor diverse microbial communities that may contribute to host-associated ecological interactions, microbial competition, and chemical defense. However, the compartment-specific organization of sea urchin-associated microbiota and their predicted chemical-defense-related functional potential remain poorly understood under aquaculture conditions. In this study, 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing was used to characterize microbial communities in rearing water, coelomic fluid, intestine, stomach contents, and surface mucus of Hemicentrotus pulcherrimus (H. pulcherrimus). KEGG Ortholo
papers.summary: This study characterizes the microbial communities living in different body compartments of cultured sea urchins (Hemicentrotus pulcherrimus), revealing distinct microbial compositions in rearing water, coelomic fluid, intestine, stomach contents, and surface mucus. The authors also predict that these compartment-specific microbiomes have different functional potentials related to chemical defense, suggesting that sea urchin-associated microbes may play specialized roles in host protection.

papers.title: Antibiotic Resistance Profiles of Bacterial Strains Isolated from the Roots, Cladodes and Rhizosphere of Opuntia dillenii (KerGawl.) Haw (Cactaceae) in the Coastal Zone of Benin.
papers.abstract: Endophytic and rhizosphere bacteria have considerable potential as bioinoculants for enhancing plant growth and improving soil health. However, despite their agricultural importance, their antibiotic resistance profiles remain poorly documented. This study assessed the antibiotic resistance of 31 bacterial strains isolated from the roots, cladodes, and rhizosphere of O. dillenii growing in the coastal zone of Benin. Antibiotic susceptibility was evaluated using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method according to CA-SFM/EUCAST guidelines. Depending on the bacterial genus, each strain was tested
papers.summary: This study assessed antibiotic resistance in 31 bacterial strains isolated from the roots, cladodes, and rhizosphere of the cactus Opuntia dillenii in Benin, finding that resistance profiles vary by bacterial genus. The work highlights that agriculturally important endophytic and rhizosphere bacteria can carry antibiotic resistance, which has implications for both plant health and public health.

papers.title: Construction of Customized Personas for Decision-Making Cognition Regarding Oral Microbiota Transplantation in Head and Neck Cancer Patients Undergoing Radiotherapy: A Qualitative Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Patients with head and neck cancer who are undergoing radiotherapy frequently suffer from oral mucositis and oral microecological disorders, which severely impair their quality of life. Oral microbiota transplantation is an emerging oral microecological intervention that offers a novel approach for reconstructing oral microecological balance and relieving mucositis. However, regarding this innovative therapy, there is a paucity of in-depth research into patients' decision-making cognition, and existing evidence is insufficient to support individualized clinical decision-making guid
papers.summary: This qualitative study explores how head and neck cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy perceive and make decisions about oral microbiota transplantation, an emerging therapy for oral mucositis and microecological disorders. The authors constructed personalized decision-making personas to better understand patient cognition and support individualized clinical guidance.

papers.title: Habitat-Dependent Ecological Differentiation of Soil and Water Microbiomes in High-Altitude Alpine Meadow Ecosystems on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau.
papers.abstract: High-altitude ecosystems are characterized by extreme environmental conditions that strongly influence microbial community structure and function. However, whether soil and water microbiomes exhibit similar ecological responses to environmental variation in alpine meadow ecosystems on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau remains poorly understood. Here, we combined 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and metagenomic sequencing to compare soil and water microbiomes across two regions (LZ and NQ) with distinct physicochemical profiles. Environmental heterogeneity was more pronounced in water habitats, wher
papers.summary: This study compares soil and water microbiomes in high-altitude alpine meadows on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau, finding that water habitats show greater environmental heterogeneity and distinct microbial community structures compared to soil. The results highlight habitat-dependent ecological differentiation, with water microbiomes being more sensitive to environmental variation.

papers.title: A Volatile Metabolomics Perspective: Interplay Between Indigenous Lactic Acid Bacteria and Aroma Development in Ripening Raw-Milk Cheese.
papers.abstract: Artisanal raw-milk cheese represents a complex biochemical ecosystem where the indigenous microbiota acts as the primary driver of the volatile profile. This study utilizes an innovative synchronized biological relay model to decipher the mechanistic interplay between the successional dynamics of indigenous lactic acid bacteria (LAB) and the temporal evolution of the volatile metabolome over a 10-week maturation period of an artisanal cow-milk cheese. Utilizing a culture-dependent approach focused on the quantitative enumeration of broad morpho-physiological groups-without species-level identi
papers.summary: This study explores how indigenous lactic acid bacteria (LAB) drive the development of aroma compounds in raw-milk cheese during a 10-week ripening period, using a synchronized biological relay model to link bacterial succession with volatile metabolome changes. The findings highlight the critical role of native LAB dynamics in shaping cheese flavor without relying on species-level identification.

papers.title: Metagenomic Insights into the Seasonal Distribution and Dissemination Risks of Biocide and Metal Resistance Genes in a Subtropical Coastal Ecosystem.
papers.abstract: The widespread use of antimicrobial biocides and metals has led to the continuous accumulation of biocide and metal resistance genes (BMRGs) in the environment. The issue is of growing concern, as it reduces the efficacy of these agents and poses a potential threat to coastal ecological security. However, the extent of coastal BMRG pollution, its transmission mechanisms, and the influence of seasonal variations on its assembly remain poorly understood. In this study, metagenomic sequencing was employed to investigate BMRGs, microbiomes, and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) within the subtropical
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to investigate how biocide and metal resistance genes (BMRGs) are distributed and spread in a subtropical coastal ecosystem, finding that seasonal variations significantly influence their abundance and transmission via mobile genetic elements. The results highlight the growing environmental pollution from antimicrobial biocides and metals, which poses risks to coastal ecological security.

papers.title: Fusarium Mycotoxins Are Frequently Detected in Oat Grains and Oat Foods and T-2, HT-2 and HT-2-Glucoside Are Highly Bioaccessible in Oat Porridge.
papers.abstract: The presence of Fusarium mycotoxins is an intractable problem in cereal production, with T-2 and HT-2 posing a particular issue in oats. This study assesses the prevalence of Fusarium mycotoxins in unprocessed and de-hulled oats and oat food products and quantifies the bioaccessibility of T-2, HT-2 and HT-2-glucoside from oat porridge in vitro. Twenty unprocessed food oat samples were de-hulled and mycotoxins quantified in unprocessed grains, hulls and groats using LC-MS/MS. Seventy-seven oat food products (40 porridge samples, 10 granola and muesli samples, 11 oat biscuits, 11 oatcakes, 5 inf
papers.summary: This study found that Fusarium mycotoxins, particularly T-2 and HT-2, are frequently present in oat grains and oat-based foods, and that these toxins are highly bioaccessible from oat porridge in laboratory digestion models. The findings highlight a potential health risk from consuming oat products contaminated with these mycotoxins.

papers.title: Tracking Gut Homeostasis: Key Taxa Transitions and Core Network Hyper-Connectivity as Early Signals of Dysbiosis.
papers.abstract: Background: Although the gut microbiota is generally recognized to remain relatively stable in healthy individuals, its taxonomic composition still undergoes subtle temporal fluctuations. To systematically characterize these dynamic variations, we adopted "enterotypes" as a macroscopic and practical metric to evaluate the structural dynamics of the intestinal microbial community. Methods: We longitudinally recruited a cohort of healthy adults and collected a total of 72 shotgun metagenomic fecal samples across approximately 40 days. All samples underwent metagenomic sequencing, and subjects we
papers.summary: This study tracked the gut microbiota of healthy adults over 40 days using metagenomic sequencing, finding that transitions between enterotypes and hyper-connectivity in core microbial networks can serve as early signals of dysbiosis. The results suggest that even in healthy individuals, subtle shifts in community structure may indicate impending imbalance.

papers.title: Mycobiome Simplification in Wheat Is Associated With the Pathogen Parastagonospora nodorum.
papers.abstract: Plant mycobiomes are essential to plant health, yet their assembly under biotic stressors such as pathogen infection remains poorly understood. Plant pathogens can influence microbial community composition through direct antagonism and suppression of host immune responses, potentially altering mycobiome composition in ways that could affect plant performance. We investigated how the wheat (Triticum aestivum L.) foliar mycobiome was associated with inoculation with the fungal pathogen Parastagonospora nodorum (Berk.) Quaedvlieg, Verkley & Crous, which can cause substantial loss of yield and gra
papers.summary: This study shows that infection of wheat leaves by the fungal pathogen Parastagonospora nodorum simplifies the leaf mycobiome, reducing fungal diversity. The findings suggest that pathogen invasion can reshape the microbial community in ways that may further impact plant health.

papers.title: Substrate-Driven Microbiome Assembly in Water Hyacinth Vermicompost: Combined 16S rRNA and Shotgun Metagenomics for Sustainable Agriculture.
papers.abstract: Substrate composition is a primary determinant of microbial succession and functional dynamics in vermicomposting systems. However, comparative insights into how biomass pre-treatment influences microbial architecture and how different sequencing approaches capture these changes remain limited. In this study, evaluation was carried out on microbial community structure and metabolic potential in vermicompost derived from three forms of Eichhornia crassipes (water hyacinth) biomass, burnt biomass (BB), composted biomass (CB) and dry biomass (DB) using both 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing and s
papers.summary: This study investigates how different pre-treatments of water hyacinth biomass (burnt, composted, or dry) shape the microbial community and functional potential in vermicompost, using both 16S rRNA and shotgun metagenomics. The findings highlight that substrate composition strongly drives microbiome assembly, with implications for optimizing sustainable agricultural practices.

papers.title: Revalorizing Cocoa Endocarp Residues as Novel Ingredients With Potential Prebiotic Effects: A Step Toward Circular Economy.
papers.abstract: The interior part of the cocoa husk, known as the cocoa endocarp, is a by-product of the chocolate sector that contains bioactive compounds with health benefits. In this research, the nutritional and physicochemical characteristics, and antioxidant capacity of dehydrated (DC) and lyophilized (LC) cocoa endocarps were evaluated, as well as their prebiotic properties affecting the human intestinal microbiota (IM). A simulated gastrointestinal digestion process was applied to DC and LC prior to 48 h of in vitro fecal fermentation. An increase in the relative abundance (RA) of beneficial intestina
papers.summary: This study investigates cocoa endocarp, a byproduct of chocolate production, as a potential prebiotic ingredient. Dehydrated and lyophilized forms were tested in simulated digestion and fecal fermentation, showing increased beneficial gut bacteria. The work supports circular economy by valorizing food waste for health-promoting applications.

papers.title: Structural Characterization and Gut Microbiota Modulation of Theabrownins Prepared by Macroporous Resin AB-8 Combined With Ultrafiltration Fractionation.
papers.abstract: This study developed an efficient and environmentally benign method using macroporous resin purification combined with ultrafiltration fractionation to prepare a high-molecular-weight theabrownin fraction (TBSP5, Mw > 100 kDa) from summer green tea fermented with Aspergillus cristatus (MK346334). TBSP5 exhibited higher purity than theabrownins obtained via conventional organic solvent extraction (TBSE) while it retained comparable structural characteristics. Both TBSP5 and TBSE showed substantial stability under simulated upper gastrointestinal digestion, undergoing only limited hydrolysis bef
papers.summary: This study developed a greener method using macroporous resin and ultrafiltration to purify high-molecular-weight theabrownins from fermented tea, yielding a fraction with higher purity than conventional solvent extraction. The purified theabrownins remained stable during simulated digestion, suggesting potential for gut microbiota modulation.

papers.title: In silico dysbiosis-associated neuroprotective metabolite insufficiency in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Perturbation of oral and gut microbiomes has been implicated in alzheimer's disease (AD) along the oral-gut-brain axis; however, the extent of global community restructuring may differ between niches. The present work constitutes a computational interrogation of 16S rRNA profiles from eight-month-old APP/PS1 and wild-type mice, characterizing oral and gut community structure and predicted functional capacity through PICRUSt-driven, KEGG-anchored pathway inference. Comparative taxonomic interrogation disclosed patterns consistent with ectopic occurrence, whereby classically oral genera (Fusobac
papers.summary: This study uses computational analysis of 16S rRNA data from Alzheimer's disease model mice to show that gut and oral microbiomes are disrupted, with oral bacteria appearing in the gut. The predicted functional analysis suggests these microbial changes lead to a deficiency in neuroprotective metabolites, potentially linking microbiome dysbiosis to Alzheimer's pathology.

papers.title: Day-21 gut microbiota community state types are associated with bronchopulmonary dysplasia classification in preterm infants: a pilot shotgun metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a major complication in preterm infants, and its clinical classification remains strongly influenced by gestational maturity and the evolving respiratory course. In this exploratory study, we investigated whether early-life gut microbiota configurations at postnatal day 21 are associated with subsequent formal BPD classification at 36 weeks postmenstrual age and whether they provide ecological information relevant to preterm infant microbiome development.
papers.summary: This pilot study found that the composition of gut bacteria in preterm infants at 21 days old is linked to their later diagnosis of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), a serious lung complication. The findings suggest that early gut microbiome patterns could help predict BPD severity and provide insights into infant development.

papers.title: A realistic simulation-based benchmark of microbiome normalization in sample stratification and taxa-level analysis.
papers.abstract: Normalization is a critical step in microbiome studies because sequencing depth and sparsity can strongly affect downstream analyses. In real datasets, however, the underlying biological signal is unknown, making it difficult to determine whether a normalization method preserves true group differences or introduces distortions. To address this problem in a way that remains relevant to real applications, we developed a simulation-based evaluation framework informed by real microbiome data. The framework generates realistic datasets with known ground truth and enables quantitative comparison of
papers.summary: This study introduces a simulation-based framework that uses real microbiome data to generate realistic datasets with known ground truth, enabling quantitative comparison of normalization methods for sample stratification and taxa-level analysis. The authors demonstrate that this approach can reveal which normalization techniques preserve true biological signals versus introducing distortions, addressing a key challenge in microbiome research where underlying signals are unknown in real data.

papers.title: Cigarette Butts as an Emerging Urban Habitat Driving Microbial Niche Differentiation.
papers.abstract: Cigarette butts are common yet overlooked pollutants in urban environments. How this anthropogenic niche shapes microbial life-history strategies and evolutionary mechanisms remains poorly understood, limiting assessments of microbial adaption and urban ecosystem health. However, systematic and multiscale evidence on the ecological effects of cigarette butts on microbial communities remains scarce. Here, we collected cigarette butts, litter, and soil samples from urban parks in 35 Chinese cities and integrated third-generation 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing, metagenomics, and transcriptomics to
papers.summary: This study investigates how discarded cigarette butts create a unique urban habitat that drives microbial niche differentiation. By analyzing samples from 35 Chinese cities using multi-omics approaches, the researchers found that cigarette butts harbor distinct microbial communities with specific life-history strategies and evolutionary adaptations compared to surrounding litter and soil.

papers.title: Functional signatures of the gut microbiome in middle-aged regular runners: insights from a metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Exercise influences host metabolism and inflammation, but its functional effects on the gut microbiome in middle-aged populations remain unclear. This study used shotgun metagenomics to investigate the associations between long-term endurance running and the gut microbial ecosystem and its functional potential in middle-aged adults.
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the gut microbiomes of middle-aged regular runners versus sedentary controls, finding that runners had distinct microbial functional profiles linked to enhanced metabolic and anti-inflammatory pathways. The results suggest that long-term endurance exercise is associated with beneficial functional changes in the gut microbiome, even in middle age.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of fecal and environmental microbiota in rural mixed livestock farming systems in South Africa.
papers.abstract: In South African rural areas, farmers often practice mixed extensive livestock farming, facilitating microbial exchange among and between animal species and their environment. The composition and transmission potential of microbiomes between animals and their environments in these smallholder livestock systems remain largely unexplored, creating a gap in understanding how mixed-livestock farming affects gut and environmental microbiomes. Shotgun metagenomics was used to uncover the fecal and environmental microbiota in smallholder mixed livestock systems, aiming to understand microbiome transf
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics to characterize the fecal and environmental microbiomes in smallholder mixed livestock farms in rural South Africa, revealing microbial exchange between animals and their surroundings. The findings fill a gap in understanding how mixed-livestock farming shapes gut and environmental microbiota in these understudied systems.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in soil microbiome-driven agriculture: from practical limits to a translational roadmap.
papers.abstract: Soil microbiome research has been revolutionized by advances in high-throughput sequencing and multi-omics technologies, generating massive datasets that capture the taxonomic, functional, and metabolic diversity of microbial communities in agricultural soils; however, interpreting these complex datasets and translating them into practical agronomic insights remains challenging.
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence can help analyze complex soil microbiome data from high-throughput sequencing and multi-omics to improve agriculture, but also highlights current limitations and outlines a roadmap for translating these insights into practical farming applications.

papers.title: The Gut-Joint Axis in Hip Osteoarthritis: Distinct Articular Microbial Profiles and Metabolic Potential Compared With Nonarthritic Controls.
papers.abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis and systemic microbial translocation potentially contribute to chronic joint inflammation. However, the role of the gut-joint axis in the genesis of osteoarthritis still needs to be elucidated. This investigation characterized taxonomic signatures and proinflammatory metabolic pathways within the hip joint to define their contribution to the pathophysiology of osteoarthritis relative to nonarthritic controls.
papers.summary: This study found distinct microbial profiles and metabolic pathways in the hip joints of osteoarthritis patients compared to nonarthritic controls, suggesting a gut-joint axis may contribute to joint inflammation. The findings indicate that bacteria or their byproducts may travel from the gut to the hip joint, potentially driving osteoarthritis pathology.

papers.title: Shared and condition-associated gut microbiota alterations in older adults with depression and constipation: evidence from the American Gut Project.
papers.abstract: Constipation and depression frequently co-occur in older adults, and growing evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis may be a shared feature of both conditions. The microbiota has well-established roles in gastrointestinal motility and gut-brain axis signaling, and compositional alterations have been independently reported in each condition. However, whether older adults with constipation and those with depression share common microbiota characteristics have not been systematically investigated.
papers.summary: This study analyzed gut microbiota data from older adults in the American Gut Project and found shared microbial alterations in those with depression and constipation, suggesting a common gut-brain axis dysbiosis. The findings indicate that specific bacterial changes may underlie the frequent co-occurrence of these conditions in aging populations.

papers.title: Age-associated gut microbiome succession, colonization resistance, and relative resistome patterns in an antibiotic-restricted infant cohort.
papers.abstract: Early infancy is critical for gut microbiome assembly and the establishment of colonization resistance against pathobionts. Whether age-associated microbiome maturation is accompanied by changes in colonization-resistance proxies and relative antimicrobial resistance gene profiles under low infant antibiotic exposure remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study tracked gut microbiome development in infants with minimal antibiotic exposure, finding that age-related microbial succession strengthens colonization resistance against harmful bacteria while reducing the relative abundance of antimicrobial resistance genes. The results suggest that natural microbiome maturation in low-antibiotic settings can enhance protective functions and limit resistome expansion.

papers.title: Fecal metagenomic profiling in patients with colorectal adenomas to characterize gut microbial composition and functional potential.
papers.abstract: To investigate differences in gut microbiota between patients with colorectal adenoma (CRA) and healthy individuals using metagenomic sequencing, and to analyze the correlation between microbial abundance and polyp diameter and number.
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing to compare the gut microbiota of patients with colorectal adenomas (precancerous polyps) to healthy individuals, finding distinct differences in microbial composition and function. The abundance of certain bacteria was correlated with polyp size and number, suggesting that gut microbes could serve as biomarkers for early detection of colorectal cancer risk.

papers.title: Microbial functional gene assembly is associated with soil carbon and nitrogen dynamics during grassland degradation.
papers.abstract: Grassland degradation is often accompanied by changes in the structure and function of soil microbial communities. However, the mechanisms by which the assembly of microbial functional communities is associated with alterations in soil carbon and nitrogen pools remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how the assembly of microbial functional genes relates to changes in soil carbon and nitrogen pools during grassland degradation. The findings reveal that shifts in microbial functional gene composition are closely linked to alterations in soil carbon and nitrogen dynamics, providing insights into the mechanisms underlying grassland degradation.

papers.title: In silico identification and biophysical characterization of candidate antimicrobial peptides from the Indian marine microbiome targeting multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens.
papers.abstract: The global health crisis of antimicrobial resistance necessitates the discovery of new antibacterial agents. Underexplored marine microbiomes, particularly from the biodiverse Indian coast, represent a rich potential source of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). Targeting the urgent threat of multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens, the present study aimed to computationally identify novel, membrane-active AMPs from these unique metagenomic datasets, with a focus on inhibiting Gram-negative bacteria. In this study, we computationally mined Indian marine high-resolution shotgun metagenomic datasets thr
papers.summary: This study computationally identified novel antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) from Indian marine metagenomes that target multidrug-resistant ESKAPE pathogens. The authors used in silico screening and biophysical characterization to discover membrane-active AMPs with potential against Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting underexplored marine microbiomes as a source of new antibiotics.

papers.title: Metagenome analysis reveals multi-kingdom gut microbiota as diagnostic markers for colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major contributor to cancer-related morbidity and mortality globally. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in CRC development. However, the precise link between CRC and gut microbial dysbiosis remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic analysis to show that multi-kingdom gut microbiota (including bacteria, fungi, and viruses) can serve as diagnostic markers for colorectal cancer. The findings suggest that analyzing the entire microbial community, not just bacteria, improves the accuracy of CRC detection.

papers.title: Urinary Microbiota in Female Patients With Dry and Wet Overactive Bladder (OAB).
papers.abstract: This study is aimed at comparing the urinary microbiota between OAB patients and healthy controls and at assessing whether urinary incontinence status affects the urinary microbiota in OAB patients.
papers.summary: This study compares the urinary microbiota of women with overactive bladder (OAB) to healthy controls, finding differences in bacterial composition between OAB subtypes (dry vs. wet) and controls. The results suggest that urinary incontinence status may influence the urinary microbiome in OAB patients.

papers.title: Paired comparison of tumor core and airway lumen (BALF) microbiomes in lung adenocarcinoma: deciphering specific Bacillus enrichment and immunomodulation.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading cause of cancer mortality. While the lung microbiome influences tumorigenesis, the spatial heterogeneity between the airway reservoir (bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, BALF) and the actual intratumoral niche remains underexplored. Understanding this distinction is critical for identifying true tumor-resident drivers.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study compares the microbiomes of tumor core tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) in lung adenocarcinoma patients, finding that Bacillus species are specifically enriched in tumors and may modulate immune responses. The results highlight the importance of distinguishing between airway and intratumoral microbiomes to identify true tumor-resident microbial drivers.

papers.title: Gut microbiota profiles in pediatric atopic dermatitis and their relationship with skin microbiota: an Indonesian case-control study.
papers.abstract: The bacterial gut microbiota has been implicated in the pathophysiology of atopic dermatitis (AD), yet most studies have focused on Western populations and have typically examined the gut or skin microbiota in isolation. Evidence for interactions between skin and gut microbiota in inflammatory skin diseases remains limited, particularly in pediatric cohorts from non-Western settings. Here, we profiled the bacterial gut microbiota in children with AD from Indonesia, and evaluated the relationship with bacterial skin microbiota using paired gut and skin samples from the same individuals.
papers.summary: This study profiles the gut microbiota of Indonesian children with atopic dermatitis and finds distinct bacterial compositions compared to healthy controls, with specific taxa linked to disease severity. By analyzing paired gut and skin samples, it reveals correlations between the two microbial communities, suggesting potential cross-talk in inflammatory skin disease. The work extends previous findings to a non-Western pediatric population, highlighting the importance of considering both gut and skin microbiota in AD.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota in Constipation and Mild Cognitive Impairment: A Mendelian Randomization and Observational Study of Two Common Geriatric Syndromes.
papers.abstract: In geriatric syndrome (GS), conditions like cognitive impairment and constipation reduce quality of life. Gut microbiota may influence GS progression via the gut-brain axis. This exploratory study investigated potential causal associations and microbial characteristics between gut microbiota and constipation, including constipation with mild cognitive impairment.
papers.summary: This study explores whether gut microbiota play a causal role in constipation and mild cognitive impairment, two common geriatric syndromes, using Mendelian randomization and observational data. The findings suggest potential microbial links via the gut-brain axis, offering insights into shared mechanisms that could inform future interventions.

papers.title: Cervical Cytological Findings and Vaginal Microbiota Alterations During Pregnancy: A Retrospective Analysis.
papers.abstract: Pregnancy induces physiological and microbiological changes in the cervicovaginal environment, which may affect the interpretation of cervical cytology. Accurate screening in this population is essential to identify both benign and pathological alterations.
papers.summary: This retrospective study examines how pregnancy alters the cervicovaginal environment, affecting cervical cytology interpretation and vaginal microbiota composition. The findings highlight the need for accurate screening to distinguish benign pregnancy-related changes from pathological alterations.

papers.title: Tripterygium glycosides tablet ameliorates chronic kidney disease via gut-derived uremic toxins reduction in rats: alkaloids as major toxic ingredients.
papers.abstract: Tripterygium glycosides tablet (TGT), the major preparation of Tripterygium wilfordii Hook. f (TWHF), is widely used in treating chronic kidney disease (CKD). However, its complex composition and overlap between active and toxic constituents often lead to adverse effects, limiting precise clinical use. This study aimed to clarify the therapeutic mechanisms of TGT in CKD and identify its potential toxic ingredients.
papers.summary: This study investigates how Tripterygium glycosides tablets (TGT) improve chronic kidney disease (CKD) in rats by reducing gut-derived uremic toxins, while identifying alkaloids as the primary toxic components. The findings help separate therapeutic effects from toxicity, potentially guiding safer clinical use of TGT.

papers.title: Clinical and immunomicrobiome correlates of a standardized Qingpao Chushi Jiedu Fang regimen in palmoplantar pustulosis.
papers.abstract: Palmoplantar pustulosis (PPP) is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis with limited therapeutic options. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formulations may benefit PPP, yet microbiome-immune mechanisms underlying clinical response remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates how a Traditional Chinese Medicine formula (Qingpao Chushi Jiedu Fang) affects palmoplantar pustulosis by examining changes in the skin microbiome and immune response. The findings suggest that clinical improvement is linked to specific shifts in microbial composition and immune markers, offering mechanistic insight into how this therapy works.
